topicName: Temporal Data Support in SQL: SQL:2011 Standard
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Temporal Data Support in SQL: SQL:2011 Standard"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The SQL:2011 standard introduced significant enhancements for handling temporal data, providing standardized ways to manage data that changes over time. This tutorial will explore the key features of temporal data support in SQL:2011, including system-versioned tables, application-time period tables, and bitemporal tables."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Temporal Data"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Temporal data refers to data that is associated with a specific period or point in time. It allows you to track changes to data over time, providing a historical record of the data's evolution.  There are two primary types of temporal data:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"System Time: Represents the time when the database recorded the data. This is managed by the database system itself."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Application Time: Represents the time when the data was actually valid in the real world. This is managed by the application."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"System-Versioned Tables (System Time)"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"System-versioned tables automatically track the history of changes made to the data. The database system manages the start and end timestamps for each row, indicating when the row was valid in the database."},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"To create a system-versioned table, use the `PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME` clause and the `SYSTEM_TIME` option."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE employees (
 employee_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
 employee_name VARCHAR(255),
 salary DECIMAL(10, 2),
 valid_from TIMESTAMP GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START,
 valid_to TIMESTAMP GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW END,
 PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME (valid_from, valid_to)
) WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING;"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example:"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`valid_from` and `valid_to` are automatically generated columns that store the start and end timestamps of each row's validity in the system."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME (valid_from, valid_to)` defines the period for system time tracking."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING` enables system versioning for the table."},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"To query historical data from a system-versioned table, use the `FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF` clause:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM employees
FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01 10:00:00';"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"This query retrieves the state of the `employees` table as it was on January 1, 2023, at 10:00:00 AM."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Application-Time Period Tables (Application Time)"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Application-time period tables allow you to manage the validity of data based on application-specific time periods.  The application is responsible for maintaining the start and end timestamps."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE products (
 product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
 product_name VARCHAR(255),
 price DECIMAL(10, 2),
 valid_from DATE,
 valid_to DATE,
 PERIOD FOR valid_period (valid_from, valid_to)
);"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example:"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`valid_from` and `valid_to` are columns that store the start and end dates of the product's validity."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`PERIOD FOR valid_period (valid_from, valid_to)` defines the period for application time tracking. Note that `SYSTEM VERSIONING` is not used here."},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"To query data valid during a specific period, use the `CONTAINS`, `OVERLAPS`, or `EQUALS` operators with the period column:"},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM products
WHERE valid_period CONTAINS DATE '2023-06-15';"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"This query retrieves all products that were valid on June 15, 2023."},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Bitemporal Tables (System and Application Time)"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"Bitemporal tables combine both system time and application time, providing a complete history of data changes and their validity in the real world. This is the most powerful, but also the most complex, temporal data management approach."},{"order":29,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE contracts (
 contract_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
 customer_name VARCHAR(255),
 contract_value DECIMAL(12, 2),
 app_valid_from DATE,
 app_valid_to DATE,
 sys_valid_from TIMESTAMP GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START,
 sys_valid_to TIMESTAMP GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW END,
 PERIOD FOR app_period (app_valid_from, app_valid_to),
 PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME (sys_valid_from, sys_valid_to)
) WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING;"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example:"},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`app_valid_from` and `app_valid_to` store the application-time validity period."},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`sys_valid_from` and `sys_valid_to` store the system-time validity period."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`PERIOD FOR app_period (app_valid_from, app_valid_to)` defines the application-time period."},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME (sys_valid_from, sys_valid_to)` defines the system-time period."},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING` enables system versioning."},{"order":36,"type":"paragraph","text":"Querying bitemporal tables requires combining conditions for both application time and system time:"},{"order":37,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM contracts
FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF TIMESTAMP '2023-08-01 12:00:00'
WHERE app_period CONTAINS DATE '2023-07-15';"},{"order":38,"type":"paragraph","text":"This query retrieves the state of the `contracts` table as it was recorded in the database on August 1, 2023, at 12:00:00 PM, but only includes contracts that were valid in the application on July 15, 2023."},{"order":39,"type":"subheading","text":"Considerations and Limitations"},{"order":40,"type":"paragraph","text":"While the SQL:2011 standard provides robust temporal data support, there are considerations to keep in mind:"},{"order":41,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Not all database systems fully implement the SQL:2011 temporal features. Check your database documentation for specific support."},{"order":42,"type":"bullet_point","text":"System-versioned tables can significantly increase storage requirements due to the historical data being maintained."},{"order":43,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Application-time period tables require careful management of the validity periods by the application."},{"order":44,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Querying temporal tables can be more complex than querying regular tables, especially for bitemporal data."},{"order":45,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":46,"type":"paragraph","text":"The SQL:2011 standard's temporal data support provides powerful tools for managing data that changes over time. By understanding system-versioned tables, application-time period tables, and bitemporal tables, you can effectively track and analyze historical data within your database systems. Remember to consult your specific database system's documentation for implementation details and supported features."}]
